item.title: Psychology in the service of the disabled, the ill and the dying
item.content:encoded:
Ami Rokach, York University

This special issue explores psychology's role in supporting individuals facing disability, illness, and mortality. Disability encompasses not only physical, sensory, or intellectual impairment but also societal exclusion and discrimination. Illness creates significant psychological stress through symptoms and hospitalization, while death and dying present unique challenges for patients and their families.

Appel publié par The Journal of Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Disability and psychology, including adjustment to loss, stigma, disability pride, and mental health disparities
  • Ableism and discrimination against people with physical or mental disabilities
  • Psychological impacts of illness, including stress, pain, fatigue, and loss of bodily functions
  • Hospitalization and its short-term and long-term psychological consequences
  • Death, dying, and end-of-life psychological support
  • Grief and bereavement support for families
  • Mental health interventions for disabled, ill, and dying individuals

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Deadline for submission of manuscript
  • January 31, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Impactful Research: Advancing Practical and Societal Relevance
item.content:encoded:
Diletta Acuti, University of Bath

Mario Campana, University of Bath

Anirban Mukhopadhyay, Bayes Business School

Jens Nordfält, University of Bath

Anne Roggeveen, Babson College

This special issue seeks scholarly research at the intersection of psychology and marketing that produces practical and societal impact. Impact is defined as research that creates positive change beyond academia by addressing real-world issues or providing clear benefits to individuals, organizations, and society. The issue welcomes research from various perspectives, including those developed through partnerships with policymakers, business leaders, nonprofit organizations, and consumer groups.

Submissions should offer rigorous analysis grounded in relevant theory while providing insights into how research can advance theory, influence practice, and address pressing societal challenges. Field-based research is particularly encouraged. The central criterion for acceptance is evidence that research generates meaningful impact on different stakeholders.

Appel publié par Psychology and Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Conceptual contributions that offer new frameworks that help practitioners or society
  • Methodological perspectives that offer new or revised methodologies to help achieve and measure real-world impact
  • Questions studied empirically from many perspectives, including, but not limited to, those of consumers, retailers, brands, policymakers, nonprofit organizations, communities, and non-human beneficiaries
  • Impact articles that offer concrete evidence that supports the impact that the research have on different stakeholders

Timeline

  • June 15, 2026: Open for Submission
  • September 15, 2026: Submission deadline
